extracted.intended_audience: citizens, lawmakers, legal practitioners, and students of constitutional law
extracted.subtask_description: Transcription of the Articles of Confederation and the United States Constitution setting out structural rules, powers, limits, and procedures for the federal government and the States. Contains enumerated powers, prohibitions, representation rules, appointment and election procedures, and procedural safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: State representation in Congress under Articles of Confederation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each State shall be represented in Congress by less than two, nor by more than seven members; no person shall be a delegate for more than three years in any six-year term; delegates may not hold any U.S. office for which they receive salary, fees, or emolument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets limits on delegation size and tenure and prohibits delegates from holding paid U.S. offices to avoid conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: State delegation maintenance and committee service
rubrics_metrics.description: Each State shall maintain its own delegates in any meeting of the States, and while they act as members of the committee of the States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires continuous representation; delegates of a State attend both full and committee meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: State equality of vote in Congress (Articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining questions in the United States in Congress assembled, each State shall have one vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms equal State voting regardless of population for Articles-era Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom of speech and debate for delegates (Articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Freedom of speech and debate in Congress shall not be impeached or questioned in any court or place out of Congress; delegates protected from arrest while attending Congress except for treason, felony, or breach of the peace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immunity for debate and certain protections against arrest to preserve legislative independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: State foreign intercourse restrictions (Articles Art. VI)
rubrics_metrics.description: No State, without the consent of the United States in Congress assembled, shall send or receive embassies, enter into agreements, alliances, or treaties with any king, prince, or state; officers under the U.S. shall not accept presents, emoluments, offices, or titles from foreign states; United States shall not grant titles of nobility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralizes foreign relations and bars foreign emoluments and titles to avoid foreign influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interstate compacts and consent requirement (Articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: No two or more States shall enter into any treaty, confederation, or alliance without the consent of the United States in Congress assembled, specifying purpose and duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires federal consent for interstate agreements to preserve national cohesion.

rubrics_metrics.name: State imposts not to interfere with treaties (Articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: No State shall lay any imposts or duties which may interfere with stipulations in treaties entered into by the United States in Congress assembled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents State trade measures from undermining federal treaty obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on State naval and military forces (Articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: No vessels of war shall be kept up in time of peace by any State except such number as deemed necessary by the United States in Congress assembled; no body of forces kept up except such as deemed requisite to garrison necessary forts; every State shall keep a well-regulated militia and maintain public stores of field-pieces, tents, arms, ammunition, and camp equipage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restricts standing State militaries in peacetime while requiring militia readiness and public war materiel.

rubrics_metrics.name: State war engagement restriction (Articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: No State shall engage in any war without the consent of the United States in Congress assembled, unless actually invaded or facing imminent Indian invasion; no State shall grant commissions to ships of war or letters of marque except after U.S. declaration of war or if invested by pirates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralizes declaration of war and privateering; allows narrow emergency exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of lower officers for state-raised land forces (Articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: When land forces are raised by any State for the common defence, officers of or under rank of colonel shall be appointed by the legislature of each State respectively or as that State directs; vacancies filled by the State which made the appointment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserves appointment of certain officers to State legislatures for State-raised troops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common treasury and state contributions (Articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: All charges of war and other expenses allowed by the United States in Congress assembled shall be defrayed out of a common treasury, supplied by the several States in proportion to the value of land within each State as estimated by Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes common funding mechanism and formula based on land values; requires State tax action to raise their share.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive federal powers (Articles Art. IX)
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States in Congress assembled shall have sole and exclusive right to determine peace and war (with some exceptions), sending and receiving ambassadors, entering into treaties and alliances (subject to provisions), making rules about captures and prizes, granting letters of marque and reprisal in peace, appointing courts for piracy and felonies on the high seas, and establishing courts for appeals in capture cases; no member of Congress shall be appointed judge of those courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates central foreign, maritime, and wartime powers and restricts dual service in Congress and courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal adjudication of interstate disputes (Articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: United States in Congress assembled shall be final resort on appeal in disputes between States concerning boundary, jurisdiction, or other causes, with prescribed petition, notice, appointment or selection of commissioners/judges (striking names and drawing lots), oath for commissioners, and requirement that majority of judges agree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribes a detailed process for interstate dispute resolution including nomination, selection by lot, oath, quorum rules, and finality of judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution of private land grant disputes between States (Articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Controversies concerning private rights of soil claimed under different grants of two or more States shall be finally determined by petition to Congress in the same manner as territorial disputes between States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extends interstate dispute resolution procedure to conflicting land grant claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal control of coinage, weights/measures, and Indian affairs (Articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress has power to regulate alloy and value of coin struck by their authority or by States, fix standards of weights and measures throughout the United States, and regulate trade and affairs with Indians not members of any State, without infringing State legislative rights within their limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralizes monetary standards, weights and measures, and Indian affairs while protecting certain State legislative prerogatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing post-offices and charging postage (Articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishing and regulating post-offices from one State to another and exacting such postage on papers as may be required to defray expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigns interstate postal system regulation and fee authority to federal Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment and regulation of armed forces and officers (Articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress shall appoint officers of the land forces (except regimental officers), appoint all officers of the naval forces, commission all officers in U.S. service, make rules for government and regulation of land and naval forces, and direct their operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralizes appointment and military governance at the federal level, subject to enumerated exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee of the States and federal committees (Articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress may appoint a Committee of the States to sit in recess consisting of one delegate from each State, and other committees and civil officers as necessary; appoint a presiding officer who shall not serve more than one year in any term of three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides for limited recess governance via an appointed committee with term limits for its presiding officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Borrowing, issuing bills, naval construction, and requisitions (Articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress may borrow money, emit bills on credit, build and equip a navy, agree upon number of land forces and make requisitions from each State in proportion to the number of white inhabitants; requisition shall be binding and the State legislature shall appoint regimental officers, raise, clothe, arm, and equip men at the expense of the United States; adjustments allowed if circumstances warrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants fiscal and military requisition powers to Congress and prescribes State responsibilities for fulfilling requisitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting thresholds for major acts (Articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain acts (engaging in war, issuing letters of marque, treaties, coining money, emitting bills, borrowing, appropriating money, agreeing number of vessels or forces, appointing commander-in-chief) require assent of nine States; other questions require majority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires supermajority (nine States) for major national decisions under the Articles; limits majority decisions otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of journals and recording of yeas and nays (Articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress shall publish the journal of proceedings monthly except parts requiring secrecy; yeas and nays of delegates of each State on any question shall be entered when desired by any delegate; delegates may be furnished transcripts for State legislatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates transparency of proceedings with specified secrecy exceptions and recordkeeping for legislative accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee of States limited powers (Articles Art. X)
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee of the States or any nine of them may execute in recess such of the powers of Congress as Congress by consent of nine States thinks expedient to vest them with, provided no power requiring nine-state voice be delegated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows limited delegation to recess committee but forbids delegation of powers that themselves require nine-state assent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of Canada and other colonies (Articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Canada acceding to the Confederation shall be admitted; no other colony shall be admitted unless agreed to by nine States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies admission procedure for new members under the Articles-era Confederation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public debts prior to Confederation (Articles)
rubrics_metrics.description: All bills of credit emitted, moneys borrowed, and debts contracted by Congress before the Confederation shall be deemed a charge against the United States and the public faith is pledged for payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms federal responsibility for pre-Confederation obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binding nature and amendment of the Articles (Articles Art. XIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every State shall abide by determinations of the United States in Congress assembled; the Articles shall be inviolably observed and the Union perpetual; no alteration shall be made unless agreed in Congress and confirmed by legislatures of every State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates obligation of State compliance and an extremely high bar for amendment—unanimous ratification by State legislatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble (Constitution)
rubrics_metrics.description: We the people ... do ordain and establish this Constitution for the United States of America to form a more perfect union, establish justice, insure domestic tranquility, provide for common defence, promote general welfare, and secure blessings of liberty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement of purposes guiding interpretation and aim of the Constitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative powers vested in Congress (Constitution Art. I Sec.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: All legislative powers herein granted shall be vested in a Congress of the United States, which shall consist of a Senate and House of Representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates bicameral national legislature and confines federal legislative power to grants in the Constitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: House of Representatives composition and qualifications (Art. I Sec.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Members chosen every second year by the people; electors have qualifications requisite for electors of the most numerous branch of State legislature; Representative must be 25, seven years a citizen, and inhabitant of the State when elected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets terms, electorate qualifications, and Representative eligibility criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apportionment and census (Art. I Sec.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Representatives and direct taxes shall be apportioned among States according to numbers determined by counting free persons and three-fifths of other persons (bracketed clause noted amended later); actual enumeration within three years of first Congress and every ten years thereafter; number of representatives not exceed one per 30,000 and each State shall have at least one Representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates decennial census-based apportionment and population-based representation limits (note: references historical three-fifths clause later amended).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filling vacancies and House officers (Art. I Sec.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: When vacancies occur, the executive shall issue writs of election; the House shall choose their speaker and other officers and have sole power of impeachment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribes vacancy mechanism and internal organization/authority of the House.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senate composition, terms, and qualifications (Art. I Sec.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Senate composed of two Senators from each State chosen by legislature for six years; seats divided into three classes so one-third chosen every second year; Senator must be 30, nine years a citizen, and inhabitant of State when elected; vacancies during legislature recess may be temporarily filled by executive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes equal State representation in Senate, staggered terms, eligibility, and temporary appointment rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vice-President and Senate officers (Art. I Sec.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vice-President shall be President of the Senate with no vote unless equally divided; Senate chooses other officers and a president pro tempore in absence of Vice-President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigns Vice-President a tie-breaking Senate role and internal organization of Senate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senate power to try impeachments (Art. I Sec.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Senate shall have the sole power to try all impeachments; when trying the President, Chief Justice presides; conviction requires concurrence of two-thirds of members present; judgment limited to removal and disqualification but criminal prosecution remains possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separates impeachment trial (Senate) from impeachment initiation (House) and limits possible consequences from impeachment judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elections and congressional sessions (Art. I Sec.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Times, places, and manner of holding elections for Senators and Representatives prescribed by State legislatures but Congress may alter except as to choosing Senators; Congress shall assemble at least once a year on first Monday in December unless by law different day appointed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocates primary electoral regulation to States with federal oversight limited; mandates at least annual congressional sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Each house judge of elections, quorum, rules, discipline (Art. I Sec.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each house is judge of its own elections, returns, and qualifications; majority constitutes a quorum to do business though smaller numbers may adjourn and compel attendance; each house may determine rules, punish disorderly behavior, and expel a member by two-thirds; keep and publish journals and enter yeas and nays when desired; neither house shall adjourn more than three days without consent of the other or to any other place than that in which both are sitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives internal self-governance, discipline, recordkeeping, and checks on adjournment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislator compensation and privileges (Art. I Sec.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Senators and Representatives shall receive compensation as ascertained by law and paid from the Treasury; privileged from arrest except for treason, felony, and breach of the peace during attendance and travel; shall not be questioned elsewhere for speech or debate in either house; restrictions on appointment to civil office created/with increased emoluments during term; officeholders under U.S. cannot be members of either house.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets pay, speech/debate privilege, arrest immunity, and incompatibility between legislative membership and certain offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Origination of revenue bills and presentment clause (Art. I Sec.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: All bills for raising revenue shall originate in the House though Senate may propose amendments; every bill passed by both houses must be presented to the President who shall sign or return with objections; veto override requires two-thirds in each house; presidential inaction for ten days (excluding Sundays) makes bill law unless Congress adjourns preventing return (pocket veto).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribes revenue origination rule and detailed presentment/veto processes including override and pocket veto.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orders/resolutions to President and effect (Art. I Sec.7 continuation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every order, resolution, or vote requiring concurrence of both houses shall be presented to the President and before taking effect must be approved or repassed over his disapproval per bill rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extends presentment requirement to concurrent resolutions/orders (except adjournment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumerated powers of Congress (Art. I Sec.8 opening)
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress shall have power to lay and collect taxes, duties, imposts, and excises to pay debts and provide for common defence and general welfare, with duties uniform throughout the U.S.; to borrow money on U.S. credit; to regulate commerce with foreign nations, among the states, and with Indian tribes; to establish naturalization and uniform bankruptcy laws; to coin money and regulate its value; to punish counterfeiting; and other powers listed below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets scope of federal legislative authority subject to specified limits (uniformity of duties, general welfare language) and enumerates commerce and fiscal powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific enumerated powers (Art. I Sec.8 continued list)
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish post-offices and post-roads; promote progress of science and useful arts by securing exclusive rights to authors and inventors (copyrights/patents); constitute inferior tribunals; define and punish piracy and felonies on high seas; declare war and grant letters of marque and reprisal; raise and support armies (no appropriation for longer than two years); provide and maintain a navy; make rules for government of land and naval forces; provide for calling forth the militia, organizing, arming, and disciplining the militia while reserving appointment of officers and training authority to States; exercise exclusive legislation over the federal district and places purchased for forts, magazines, arsenals, dockyards; make all laws necessary and proper for carrying into execution foregoing powers and other powers vested by the Constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains detailed federal powers over postal service, intellectual property, judiciary, maritime crimes, war, armed forces, militia, federal district, and the Necessary and Proper Clause enabling execution of enumerated powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Migration/importation and slave trade temporal limitation (Art. I Sec.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Migration or importation of persons any State admits shall not be prohibited by Congress prior to 1808, but a tax or duty not exceeding ten dollars per person may be imposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical clause limiting Congress's power to ban the international slave trade until 1808 and permitting a modest import tax (note: historically significant and amended by later constitutional amendments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Habeas corpus suspension clause (Art. I Sec.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Privileges of the writ of habeas corpus shall not be suspended unless in cases of rebellion or invasion when public safety may require it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects personal liberty by default; allows suspension only in extreme circumstances subject to public-safety justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on bills of attainder and ex post facto laws (Art. I Sec.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: No bill of attainder or ex post facto law shall be passed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bars legislative imposition of punishment without trial and retroactive criminal laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct tax apportionment rule (Art. I Sec.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: No capitation or other direct tax shall be laid unless in proportion to the census or enumeration directed to be taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires apportionment of direct taxes among the States by population rather than equal per-state tax.

rubrics_metrics.name: No export taxes and no preference to ports (Art. I Sec.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: No tax or duty shall be laid on articles exported from any State; no preference by regulation of commerce or revenue to the ports of one State over another; vessels bound to or from one State not obliged to enter, clear, or pay duties in another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents export taxes and discrimination among ports and imposes free harbor transit between States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriations and public accounts (Art. I Sec.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: No money shall be drawn from the Treasury but in consequence of appropriations made by law; a regular statement and account of receipts and expenditures of public money shall be published from time to time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires legislative appropriation for spending and mandates public accounting for fiscal transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: No titles of nobility and emoluments restriction (Art. I Sec.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: No title of nobility shall be granted by the United States; no person holding office shall, without consent of Congress, accept any present, emolument, office, or title from any king, prince, or foreign state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents creation of nobility and foreign emoluments that could influence officeholders without congressional consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: State restrictions on treaty, coinage, and monetary instruments (Art. I Sec.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: No State shall enter into any treaty, alliance, or confederation; grant letters of marque and reprisal; coin money; emit bills of credit; make anything but gold and silver coin a tender in payment of debts; pass bills of attainder, ex post facto laws, or laws impairing contracts, or grant titles of nobility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits States from undertaking sovereign acts reserved to the federal government and from monetary and certain legislative actions that would conflict with national uniformity and contract stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: State limits on imposts, duties, and military (Art. I Sec.10 continued)
rubrics_metrics.description: No State shall, without consent of Congress, lay imposts or duties on imports or exports except necessary for inspection laws; net produce shall be for the use of the U.S. Treasury and subject to Congress revision and control; no State shall, without consent, lay duty of tonnage, keep troops or ships of war in peacetime, enter into agreements with other States or foreign powers, or engage in war unless actually invaded or in imminent danger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further constrains State fiscal and military autonomy and subjects certain State taxation to federal control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive power vested in the President (Art. II Sec.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The executive power shall be vested in a President of the United States of America who shall hold office during four years together with the Vice-President, elected as follows (electoral process described).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a single executive with fixed four-year term and pairs the office with a Vice-President selected under the electoral provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and qualifications of electors (Art. II Sec.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each State shall appoint electors in such manner as the legislature thereof may direct, equal to the whole number of Senators and Representatives to which the State may be entitled; no Senator, Representative, or person holding an office of trust or profit under the United States shall be appointed an elector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives State legislatures authority to determine elector selection method and prohibits current federal officeholders from being electors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original electoral college process (bracketed) (Art. II Sec.1 bracketed)
rubrics_metrics.description: (Bracketed historical text) Electors meet in their States and vote for two persons; make list of persons voted for and number of votes; transmit sealed to President of the Senate; person with greatest number (majority) is President; House chooses among top if no majority; Vice-President is person with next greatest; procedures for counting and contingencies described.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records original, now-amended electoral college mechanism (bracketed to indicate later amendment by the Twelfth Amendment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional power to set time for electors (Art. II Sec.1 end)
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress may determine the time of choosing the electors and the day on which they shall give their votes, which day shall be the same throughout the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserves scheduling of the electoral process to federal law to ensure uniformity across States.
